# Convert 'trans_date_trans_time' and 'dob' to datetime
df['trans_date_trans_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df['trans_date_trans_time'])
df['dob'] = pd.to_datetime(df['dob'])
In [559]:
# Calculate age
today = datetime.now()
df['age'] = today.year - df['dob'].dt.year

# Adjust for birthdate not yet reached this year
df['age'] = df['age'] - ((df['dob'].dt.month > today.month) | 
                         ((df['dob'].dt.month == today.month) & (df['dob'].dt.day > today.day))).astype(int)

# Drop the 'dob' column
df = df.drop(columns=['dob'])
In [560]:
# Calculate z-scores for each numeric column
z_scores = zscore(df.select_dtypes(include=['float64', 'int64']))

# Define threshold for outlier detection (e.g., z-score > 3 or < -3)
threshold = 3

# Boolean array indicating outliers
outlier_mask = (abs(z_scores) > threshold).any(axis=1)

# Filter rows without outliers
cleaned_df = df[~outlier_mask]

# Display cleaned dataset
print("Cleaned Dataset without outliers:")
cleaned_df.head()

In [561]:
# Define valid ranges for latitude and longitude
valid_latitude_range = (-90, 90)
valid_longitude_range = (-180, 180)

# Function to clean latitude and longitude columns
def clean_lat_long(value, valid_range):
    try:
        numeric_value = float(value)
        if valid_range[0] <= numeric_value <= valid_range[1]:
            return numeric_value
        else:
            return np.nan
    except ValueError:
        return np.nan

# Clean Latitude column
df['lat'] = df['lat'].apply(lambda x: clean_lat_long(x, valid_latitude_range))

# Clean Longitude column
df['long'] = df['long'].apply(lambda x: clean_lat_long(x, valid_longitude_range))
# Use cleaned_df instead of df for the cleaned DataFrame
cleaned_df = df.copy()
In [562]:
# Clean city population column
def clean_city_population(value):
    try:
        value = int(value)
        return value if value >= 0 else np.nan
    except ValueError:
        return np.nan

df['city_pop'] = df['city_pop'].apply(clean_city_population)

# Clean city names
def clean_city_name(city):
    try:
        return city.title() if isinstance(city, str) else np.nan
    except AttributeError:
        return np.nan

df['city'] = df['city'].apply(clean_city_name)

# Create a cleaned DataFrame
cleaned_df = df.copy()

Top five merchants by the number of transactions¶

In [526]:
# Aggregate transactions by merchant for both fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions
merchant_fraud_counts = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 1]['merchant'].value_counts().reset_index()
merchant_fraud_counts.columns = ['Merchant', 'Number of Fraudulent Transactions']

merchant_non_fraud_counts = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 0]['merchant'].value_counts().reset_index()
merchant_non_fraud_counts.columns = ['Merchant', 'Number of Non-Fraudulent Transactions']

# Select top five merchants by transaction count for both fraudulent and non-fraudulent transactions
top_fraud_merchants = merchant_fraud_counts.head(5)
top_non_fraud_merchants = merchant_non_fraud_counts.head(5)

# Identify common merchants
common_merchants = set(top_fraud_merchants['Merchant']).intersection(set(top_non_fraud_merchants['Merchant']))

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))

# Plot for fraudulent transactions
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
sns.barplot(x='Number of Fraudulent Transactions', y='Merchant', data=top_fraud_merchants)
plt.xlabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.ylabel('Merchant')
plt.title('Top Merchants by Number of Fraudulent Transactions')

# Plot for non-fraudulent transactions
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
sns.barplot(x='Number of Non-Fraudulent Transactions', y='Merchant', data=top_non_fraud_merchants)
plt.xlabel('Number of Non-Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.ylabel('Merchant')
plt.title('Top Merchants by Number of Non-Fraudulent Transactions')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

)

plt.show()

# Filter for fraud transactions
fraud_df = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 1]

# Count fraud transactions by gender_encoded
fraud_gender_counts = fraud_df['gender_encoded'].value_counts().reset_index()
fraud_gender_counts.columns = ['Gender', 'Number of Fraudulent Transactions']

# Map gender codes to readable labels
fraud_gender_counts['Gender'] = fraud_gender_counts['Gender'].map({0: 'Male', 1: 'Female'})

# Plotting the distribution of fraudulent transactions by gender
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.barplot(x='Gender', y='Number of Fraudulent Transactions', data=fraud_gender_counts, hue='Gender', palette={'Male': 'skyblue', 'Female': 'lightcoral'})
plt.xlabel('Gender')
plt.ylabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.title('Distribution of Fraudulent Transactions by Gender')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# Filter for non-fraud transactions
non_fraud_df = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 0]

# Count non-fraud transactions by gender_encoded
non_fraud_gender_counts = non_fraud_df['gender_encoded'].value_counts().reset_index()
non_fraud_gender_counts.columns = ['Gender', 'Number of Non-Fraudulent Transactions']

# Map gender codes to readable labels
non_fraud_gender_counts['Gender'] = non_fraud_gender_counts['Gender'].map({0: 'Male', 1: 'Female'})

# Plotting the distribution of non-fraudulent transactions by gender

Fraudulent transactions according to days¶

In [576]:
# Ensure 'Day_of_Week' column is created in cleaned_df
cleaned_df.loc[:, 'Day_of_Week'] = cleaned_df['trans_date_trans_time'].dt.day_name()

# Count fraudulent transactions by day of the week and ensure days are in correct order
fraud_count_by_day = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 1]['Day_of_Week'].value_counts().reindex(
    ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
).fillna(0)

# Define custom colors for each day of the week
colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd', '#8c564b', '#e377c2']

# Plotting the distribution of fraudulent transactions by day of the week
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
bars = plt.bar(x=fraud_count_by_day.index, height=fraud_count_by_day.values, color=colors)
plt.title('Fraudulent Transactions by Day of the Week')
plt.xlabel('Day of the Week')
plt.ylabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()

plt.show()

Fraud Transactions based on age¶

In [607]:
# Define age bins
bins = [0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100]
labels = ['0-20', '21-40', '41-60', '61-80', '81+']

# Ensure 'fraud_df' is a copy to avoid SettingWithCopyWarning
fraud_df = fraud_df.copy()

# Create age groups
fraud_df['Age_Group'] = pd.cut(fraud_df['age'], bins=bins, labels=labels, right=False)

# Count fraudulent transactions by age group
age_group_counts = fraud_df['Age_Group'].value_counts().reindex(labels)

# Define colors for each age group
colors = ['#1f77b4', '#ff7f0e', '#2ca02c', '#d62728', '#9467bd']

# Plotting
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.bar(age_group_counts.index, age_group_counts.values, color=colors)
plt.title('Fraudulent Transactions by Age Group')
plt.xlabel('Age Group')
plt.ylabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

cleaned_df['trans_date_trans_time'] = pd.to_datetime(cleaned_df['trans_date_trans_time'])
cleaned_df['trans_Year'] = cleaned_df['trans_date_trans_time'].dt.year

# Create a copy of the DataFrame for fraudulent transactions

# Create the figure and subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(15, 5))

# Plot: Number of Fraudulent Transactions by Year
plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
sns.countplot(x='trans_Year', data=cleaned_df_fraud, hue='trans_Year', palette={2019: 'skyblue', 2020: 'lightcoral'})
plt.title('Fraudulent Transactions by Year')
plt.xlabel('Year')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=0)

# Plot: Monthly Distribution of Fraudulent Transactions
plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
cleaned_df_fraud['Month'] = cleaned_df_fraud['trans_date_trans_time'].dt.to_period('M')  # Convert to Period for monthly counts
monthly_counts = cleaned_df_fraud['Month'].value_counts().sort_index()
sns.barplot(x=monthly_counts.index.astype(str), y=monthly_counts.values, color='royalblue')
plt.title('Monthly Fraudulent Transactions')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)

# Layout adjustment
fig.tight_layout()

# Show the plots
plt.show()

# Ensure 'cleaned_df' is properly filtered for fraudulent transactions
df_fraud = cleaned_df[cleaned_df['is_fraud'] == 1].copy()

# Check if 'state' column exists
if 'state' in df_fraud.columns:
    # Replace state abbreviations with full names
    df_fraud['state'] = df_fraud['state'].map(state_name_mapping)

    # Calculate the total amount and number of fraudulent transactions per state
    state_amount = df_fraud.groupby('state')['amt'].sum()
    state_count = df_fraud.groupby('state').size()

    fig, ax1 = plt.subplots(figsize=(15, 6))

    # Plot number of fraudulent transactions
    color = 'tab:green'
    ax1.set_xlabel('State')
    ax1.set_ylabel('Number of Fraudulent Transactions', color=color)
    bars = ax1.bar(state_count.index, state_count.values, color=color)
    ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color)

    # Rotate x-axis labels
    ax1.set_xticks(state_count.index)  # Set the ticks to match the bars
    ax1.set_xticklabels(state_count.index, rotation=90)  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability

    # Create a second y-axis for the total amount
    ax2 = ax1.twinx()  
    color = 'tab:orange'
    ax2.set_ylabel('Total Amount ($)', color=color)  
    ax2.plot(state_amount.index, state_amount.values, color=color, marker='o', linestyle='--', linewidth=2)
    ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelcolor=color)

    # Title and Layout
    plt.title('Fraudulent Transactions by State: Total Amount and Number of Transactions')
    fig.tight_layout()

    plt.show()
